mainEntity.name: Does an import change my register automatically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to let it. By default every import queues as a proposed change-set — current value beside new value, cell by cell — and you approve what lands. You can raise the bar to review every value, or lower it to auto-apply and rely on versioning to undo. Only the cells you approve are patched into your own workbook.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which values to check?

acceptedAnswer.text: The parser flags its own uncertainty. Any cell it wasn't sure of — or a heat input it computed — is shaded amber and surfaced for review, while confident reads stay quiet, so your attention goes exactly where it's needed.

mainEntity.name: Can I correct a value during review?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fix any value inline, or add a row for a field the parser missed, then approve. What lands is what you signed off on — you are never forced to accept the parser's raw read or reject the whole set.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a WPS changes after its values landed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drift detection catches it: the app tells you the register is out of sync with the library and offers to re-sync the affected rows as a fresh change-set, reviewed and approved like any other — the sheet never quietly drifts from the documents behind it.

mainEntity.name: Does it rebuild my whole spreadsheet?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. WPS Manager patches only the approved cells into your own workbook and leaves everything else exactly as you had it. Your file is never regenerated from a model, and every approved change-set is versioned so you can roll back.

mainEntity.name: What if an import has nothing to change, only something to verify?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is closed with a mark-reviewed rather than an approval that would write an identical new version — so a verification-only change-set doesn't leave you stuck between approving a change that isn't there and rejecting a correct read.
